name: zstd-concatenated-frames
description: A zstd body emitted as two concatenated frames decodes to the whole plaintext, the same way a multi-member gzip body does.
grounding: The zstd format permits frames to be concatenated, and the rule is the one `gzip-concatenated-members` pins, stated for the corpus's other real coding: a decoder consumes the whole body, not its first frame. It is a separate case rather than a note on the gzip one because the two codings are decoded by unrelated libraries on both sides, so agreement here is not implied by agreement there — and because a rule pinned for only one coding is a rule the next binding swap can quietly drop for the other.
notes: Unlike the gzip case, this one pins agreement rather than repairing a divergence: both implementations already read the second frame — Go through `klauspost/compress/zstd`, Rust through the `zstd` crate's streaming `read::Decoder`, which wraps libzstd's own multi-frame behaviour. Neither needed a multi-frame opt-in, which is exactly why nothing would have noticed if one of them lost it.
